findings.explanation: The consumed input paths, analysis, manuscript and archived environment form one nested root. Root .gitmodules leads to raw data, labels and the algorithm; load_anderson follows the algorithm module into its evaluation dataset. The unrelated upstream acquisition URL does not move the consumed BIDS files outside that boundary.

Pinned input links are present, including root -> remodnav -> Andersson evaluation data. The raw-data module also retains a host-local acquisition URL, but the paper consumes its delivered BIDS data. No permitted recipient retrieval establishes availability of those consumed payloads, so not-checked is justified rather than a fabricated retrieval failure.

The environment explicitly installs analysis and manuscript tools and the algorithm is a root gitlink. The method accepts installable package declarations as inclusion; it does not require vendoring Docker and DataLad themselves.
The retained Git tree identifies tracked source, manuscript and configuration blobs. Missing material in this deliberately incomplete capture is not evidence of untracked original work.

The two large image layers have annex pointer entries and content identities, while metadata stays in Git. The raw-data README separately specifies annex-managed payloads. Actual payload retrieval is unnecessary to identify this version-control mechanism.

The completed main run identifies image input, actions and results. However, quality_stats is absent from command dispatch, velhist remains in the manuscript, and its path history has ordinary commits rather than an environment-linked run. The linked labels run records compute_all.sh but no exact environment. Partial is supported by specific coverage gaps.

Installation and use instructions exist, but the promise to recompute every figure exceeds the documented command: its flags never dispatch quality_stats. The native rule on conflicting documentation and mechanism supports partial despite the presence of a README.

The starting point is concrete and the results-containerized tag resolves to the cited run. It does not regenerate the velocity histogram, so partial correctly distinguishes a usable starting point from the broader reproduction promise.

The paper route uses root-relative input paths. The explicitly linked labels documentation still directs readers to Condor generation, whose retained submit scripts embed a user-specific working directory and Python 2.7 executable. That makes the scoped partial finding concrete, rather than counting container-internal paths as host defects.

Direct analysis imports and manuscript commands match the declared scientific packages and tools. DataLad has an explicit optional import fallback because host-side input provisioning is recorded. Minor citation-description correction: remodnav.tests.utils also imports pandas and pylab inside helpers; both are covered by this environment, so the verdict does not change.
findings.suggested_correction: Correct the abbreviated utils.py dependency description to include its function-local pandas and pylab imports.

Partial is supported as a documentation finding; it is not an observed permission failure.

There is a readable host-tool list plus a system/scientific package recipe. This narrower requirement can be met even though the separate all-host-assumptions criterion identifies a permissions-documentation gap.
Recipe, execution registration and saved-image metadata are tracked in the same root as the scientific code. Source inspection and tree metadata directly establish the requested versioning property.

The historical migration states a runnable build command, the build/save action is recorded, and the later OCI conversion records an actual environment-maintenance instance. This exceeds a one-time initial declaration under the native process rule. The duplicate flag with should/008 is correct. The historical Dockerfile diff itself was unavailable without fetching, so that extra supporting detail remains unchecked.

A remodnav:latest label inside the archived manifest does not select a floating registry image; unpinned recipe rebuilds are a separate issue.

The archive identities and annex web-location records establish where content is claimed to reside, not successful independent access. The study forbids payload acquisition and network checks. Retaining not-checked correctly preserves this uncertainty.

The README gives tool installation pointers, cloning, tagged replay and containerized manuscript commands, backed by a registered local image route. The old virtualenv route is explicitly labelled. The specific environment-obtainment/use property is supported; the all-figure coverage defect is already addressed under the reproduction-entry criteria.
Root and linked components use Git identities; DataLad/git-annex extends that system for bulk content. Distinct repositories do not constitute incompatible version-control systems.

The retained records provide episodic successful execution, but the all-figure instruction remains inaccurate. Library Travis configuration is not evidence of recurring full-paper verification. Partial is justified without asserting that every uncaptured external test was absent.

Raw recordings, processed labels, independent algorithm code, paper analysis and archived environment have distinguishable paths and dataset boundaries. The labels module separately nests its raw input and algorithm dependencies.

evidence: .cache/objects/paper-remodnav/evidence/external/datalad-container-1.2.3-docker.py (SHA256 44cb66ceffafe89128cdf9ec5446d035ba7b5ee39dfbf9f8754408ebfef093e5; discovery: root README DataLad Containers v1.2.3 -> .datalad/config docker adapter)
findings.explanation: A new --rm container is created, but the claimed temporary HOME is /tmp/dockertmp under the adapter's host-workspace mount at /tmp. Cleanup occurs only after make succeeds. Following a failed run, the fixed host directory survives; the next mkdir failure is followed by a semicolon, so execution can reuse that HOME. This is a specific isolation gap visible statically, not an observed failed run.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to partial: the container filesystem is disposable, but HOME can persist across failed invocations. Recommend a unique per-run HOME outside the persistent workspace or unconditional cleanup with failure handling.

findings.explanation: The 2023 recomputation and 2025 load/conversion demonstrate actual environment reuse checks. They provide some coverage, while no recurring process is established in the retained workflow and current OCI conversion is only a smoke test. Partial accurately limits the claim.

Image build/save and subsequent conversion records identify environment artifacts stored within the research object. Annex-backed layer storage still counts as archiving. Missing capture payloads limit byte verification and current access, not the evidenced archival mechanism.

This repeats must/014 by the pinned checklist design. Runnable maintenance actions and later recorded environment updates support met, and the upstream-duplicate flag makes the repeated judgment explicit.

The consumed dataset advertises unrestricted access and the algorithm is presented as openly licensed. No access-restricted component is identified in the paper analysis route; a host-local historical URL alone does not establish an access restriction. The empty-subject N/A is justified.

Independent components are linked, but the explicitly discovered upstream raw-acquisition module has a host-specific URL. Partial preserves both the working modular design and this concrete recursive link defect without alleging an observed download failure. Ordinary Python packages are correctly excluded from the module subject.

The root explains broad component roles, while the linked labels reproduction guide names scripts absent from its pinned inventory and does not describe the recorded compute_all.sh route. This limits documentation of component relationships and reuse even though the structure itself is inspectable.

Separate repositories, stable relative paths and focused pointer updates support independently maintained boundaries. The assessment appropriately avoids claiming arbitrary future updates are guaranteed to preserve numerical behavior.

The gitlinks assemble independent components and the container registration plus recorded inputs/outputs provides an explicit execution composition. A stale recursive URL is a link-quality limitation, not absence of a composition mechanism.

The criterion asks for documentation OR tooling supporting navigation. Nested Git/DataLad module paths, repository URLs and pinned identities already provide that tooling, and the assessment itself recognizes deterministic navigation. The obsolete label-generation prose limits documentation quality under may/002, but does not negate the alternative tooling route here.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to met based on Git/DataLad module navigation. Retain the stale reproduction-guide finding under may/002 and the execution/documentation criteria rather than requiring both tooling and a complete guide.

limitations: Inspection only: no scientific workflow execution, container build, payload acquisition, network request or recipient retrieval. Archived run records are historical evidence, not newly observed execution or scientific validation.

The frozen manifest hash matched the assigned hash. All 260 retained source files, seven histories, the external adapter and eight availability metadata files matched their recorded hashes. Payloads and original working-tree state are absent by design.

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 was used for every Git read. The historical 92dbad2 Dockerfile diff could not be read because an old blob is omitted; no fetch occurred. Current source, retained commit narrative and separate completed maintenance records were available.

Only the assigned anonymized JSON was reviewed. Its original probe receipts and human report were not supplied as review inputs and were not consulted; exact probe-output narratives and any report-only denominator formatting therefore remain unverified.

Native pin check and response validator passed, independently of substantive judgments. The response has exactly 31 criteria: MUST 10 met, 5 partial, 2 not-checked of 17; SHOULD 6 met, 2 partial, 1 not-applicable of 9; MAY 2 met, 3 partial of 5. No inconsistent numeric score or value mapping was present in the assigned JSON.

Public commit URLs identify immutable source revisions. The adapter is additionally cited by its frozen relative locator and SHA256 because the supplied upstream locator uses a release tag. Discovery followed root documentation, root and nested module links, and native history.
No author identity or actual model runtime identity was inferred. Agreement in this independent review is not human approval.
